title: Becoming less fun
content: A lot of changes have been coming out rapidly that seem to be almost deliberately making the game much less fun to play. “Other players” spawn in much slower and less frequently, the speed boost for kills has been totally nerfed. author: crosspumpkin
title: Poor Game
content:
Despite the game advertising as multiplayer, its features a massive amount of bots. I can play 15 games in a row with people who have the same exact profile pictures and habits. For a game with millions of downloads I don’t understand why bots are necessary and used as the main source of competition rather than other real players. Also every game almost you will unlock a new skin, but you can’t set or keep the skin you want on because every time you get a new one, it automatically equips it and you have to change it back. The game without constant predatory ads costs $10 dollars, an absolutely ridiculous amount of money for a mostly offline game that lacks in variety. A major hurdle every game tends to be the fact that you can’t set immediately join and instantly die if it spawns you next to someone who’s coming at you and you’re not prepared. It also doesn’t make sense to have new players join when another player has 80% of the map covered, they are almost guaranteed to win anyways so why put people in an unfair losing position?

7/10 Gameplay
9/10 Graphics
0/10 Trustworthiness
5/10 Replayability

author: Maugdofvjdrhrbdhdjdhchfb
title: Worst game ever
content:
Paper.io 2 starts with a simple, addictive premise: claim as much territory as possible while eliminating rival players. On the surface, it looks like a fun, competitive multiplayer game. However, a deeper look at its mechanics, connectivity issues, and intrusive monetization reveals that Paper.io 2 is a frustratingly flawed experience designed more around ad revenue than player enjoyment.
The most egregious issue with Paper.io 2 is its deceptive multiplayer structure. The game heavily implies that you are competing live against other real people. In reality, the vast majority of your "opponents" are bots programmed with predictable patterns or unfair reflexes. This fake multiplayer setup removes any real sense of achievement when taking over the map, as you are rarely outsmarting actual humans. Furthermore, when connection issues do occur, the game suffers from erratic lag spikes that instantly kill your character through no fault of your own, making gameplay feel entirely unfair.
Even if you look past the bot-filled lobbies and lag, the overall core loop is severely balanced against the player. The controls are famously sensitive and clunky, causing tiny accidental movements that snap your own line and eliminate you instantly. Because the game rewards aggressive expansion, a single small control hiccup after spending ten minutes building up a kingdom resets all your progress to zero in a second. This design creates high frustration rather than a rewarding challenge.
Finally, the monetization and advertisement model destroys whatever fun remains. Paper.io 2 is saturated with ads. You are forced to watch video ads between almost every quick round, after accidental deaths, and to unlock basic skins or revives. The game repeatedly interrupts its own gameplay flow to force commercials onto the player, making it clear that keeping users in an ad loop is a higher priority than delivering a quality gaming experience.
In conclusion, Paper.io 2 falls far short of being a good game. Between its deceptive use of bots, frustratingly finicky controls, unpredictable lag, and relentless barrage of forced advertisements, it transforms a promising arcade concept into a tedious, ad-driven cash grab.
